title: BGE-M3 CPU Encoder Benchmark on Existing Azure VM
verdict_rationale: BGE-M3 rev 5617a9f loaded successfully on CPU in an isolated venv; encoder latency measured (per-query p95 313ms, p99 326ms); determinism exact (max_abs_diff 0.0); embedding dim 1024 L2-normalized matches the index; frozen retrieval benchmark reproduced EXACTLY with the real encoder (H3 unit@5 0.5385, src@5 0.9783); end-to-end H3_RRF20 latency measured (p50 1032ms, p95 2069ms, p99 2497ms). Task-79's encoder-latency blocker is RESOLVED. The p95 gate is a marginal FAIL (+69ms / +3.5% over the 2s target), driven by BM25 full-scan variance (encoder contributes only ~300ms), reported honestly as a gate assessment; the encoder benchmark itself passed.

environment_and_dependencies.isolated_venv: /home/azureuser/.venvs/task80-bge (separate from fpvenv and all application envs)
environment_and_dependencies.torch: 2.14.1+cpu (CPU-only build; torch.cuda.is_available()=False; no CUDA packages installed)
environment_and_dependencies.thread_policy: torch threads bounded to 2 (physical cores) to protect the running application (OpenCode + uvicorn orchestrator + ollama)

model_artifacts.normalization: L2 (normalize_embeddings=True); verified l2_norm=1.0 on first embedding

secondary_cached_revision.reason: transformers/sentence-transformers prefer model.safetensors and auto-fetched it from PR #130 even though the pinned revision 5617a9f ships pytorch_model.bin. Side-effect of the loader's safetensors preference, NOT a revision change.
secondary_cached_revision.note: The effective encoder is the pinned 5617a9f (pytorch_model.bin); verified by EXACT frozen-benchmark reproduction. This extra file only inflates the cache footprint and can be deleted in cleanup.

install_and_download_footprint.model_cache_note: du -shL (follow symlinks, dedupe hardlinks) = ~4.3 GB = pytorch_model.bin (2166 MB, rev 5617a9f) + model.safetensors (2166 MB, PR #130 rev 9a0624b) + tokenizer (16 MB) + sentencepiece (5 MB) + configs. Total download ~4.25 GB (both revisions auto-cached).
install_and_download_footprint.first_load_note: smoke run performed the ~4.25 GB download + first init in ~25.1s; subsequent loads (cached) ~2.9s

warm_per_query_all47.note: 3 iters x 47 frozen queries, one-at-a-time; representative multilingual mix (34 EN, 8 Devanagari/Prakrit, 5 GUJ)

cpu_utilization.note: system load ~2.2 during encoding, matching the 2 bounded torch threads (≈2 cores busy). Per-process CPU% sampler was mis-instrumented (summed all PIDs) and is not reported as reliable.

bm25_full_s.note: BM25 full scan dominates tail variance

service_level_h3_all47.note: REAL encoder + BM25 + dense + fusion + contract validation; end-to-end

peak_memory.note: encoder (841 MB after load) + corpus + BM25 + dense index + service; measured while OpenCode + uvicorn + ollama were running

task78_gate_assessment.evidence: Service-level H3_RRF20 end-to-end p95 = 2069.36ms (real encoder), +69ms / +3.5% over the 2s gate. Marginal. Dominated by BM25 full-scan tail variance (bm25 p95 828ms); encoder contributes only ~313ms p95. Threshold NOT changed to force a pass.
corpus 5.74 + bm25 57.8 + dense 1.62 + encoder cached load 2.91 ≈ 68s (with download, first-ever load was ~25s encoder + 65s retrieval ≈ 90s, still under 120s).

task78_gate_assessment.hardware_note: The gate's 12 GB host assumption does NOT apply: this VM (Standard_B4as_v2) has 15.6 GiB total / ~12 GiB available during the run. Measured 4.04 GB is far below the 8 GB ceiling regardless of host size; recommend keeping 8 GB RSS as a safety cap.

task78_gate_assessment.evidence: Azure free credit is finite/expiring; VM+disk+IP are billable; credit balance/expiration not readable via available CLI/API (same as Task 79). Not a sustainable Rs.0 guarantee. Benchmark itself added no new cloud charge (ran on the already-provisioned VM).

blockers.blocker: End-to-end H3 p95 = 2069ms exceeds the 2s gate by 3.5%; driven by BM25 full-scan tail variance (p95 828ms), not the encoder.
blockers.impact: p95 gate FAIL (marginal). p99 gate PASS.
blockers.resolution: Candidate: cap the BM25 candidate pool (policy [retrieval] pool=2000 already reduces this vs full-scan; the service full-scan path used here is the unbounded INF path) or bound BM25 latency. Requires a separately authorized policy/perf change; not done here.

blockers.blocker: Free credit finite/expiring; balance not readable via available APIs.
blockers.impact: Rs.0 cost gate UNRESOLVED; not a sustainable guarantee.
blockers.resolution: User confirms billing setup, credit balance/expiry, post-credit plan in Azure portal.

blockers.blocker: No Qwen3-8B-Base inference serving implementation exists (training code only; re-verified).
blockers.impact: Full Qwen assistant NOT feasible; generation gate remains UNRESOLVED.
blockers.resolution: Separate task to build/evaluate an inference path (out of scope; 2-core VM CPU also impractical for 8B).

reproducibility.determinism: torch.set_num_threads(2); CPU float32 inference is deterministic (verified max_abs_diff 0.0)

cleanup_procedure: Delete the task venv: rm -rf /home/azureuser/.venvs/task80-bge   (reclaims ~1.4 GB)
Delete the bge-m3 model cache: rm -rf ~/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--BAAI--bge-m3   (reclaims ~4.3 GB, both revisions)
Optionally keep the measurements JSON and script for provenance; delete only the venv + model cache to reclaim ~5.7 GB total.
No production config, frozen artifact, or application environment is touched by cleanup.
